barrelHeader: // `src/ai.js` re-exports this file, so importing "./ai.js" still yields the
// same public surface. Only `public` symbols cross this boundary:
//   content.js   message content -> provider wire shapes

header: // Provider error taxonomy: turn an opaque network/provider failure into one
// of a fixed set of categories, and map that category to text the user can
// actually act on. Kept dependency-free so every other module can import it.
// Internal content -> provider wire shapes. The contract is documented on
// `toOpenAIContent` below; `toAnthropicContent` reshapes the same internal
// form for the Anthropic Messages API.
// OpenAI-compatible provider: /chat/completions (buffered and streamed) and
// the paginated /models listing. Covers OpenAI itself, OpenRouter, Groq,
// Together, Fireworks, DeepSeek, Ollama and anything else speaking the same
// dialect.
// Anthropic Messages API. System prompts are lifted out of the message list
// into the top-level `system` field, and the SSE event names differ from the
// OpenAI dialect, so this is a genuinely separate adapter rather than a
// configuration of openai.js.
// Streaming dispatch. Credentials are decrypted once here, and a stall
// watchdog aborts the request if the provider stops emitting for too long —
// a hung SSE connection would otherwise burn the entire fallback budget.
// Model listing and connection testing. `testConnectionRaw` deliberately
// races the provider call against a hard timeout: a provider that accepts the
// TCP connection and then never answers would otherwise hang the admin UI.
// Fallback orchestration. `tryStreamWithFallback` is the only streaming entry
// point the rest of the app uses: it resolves the user's route (or, failing
// that, their ordered connections), walks the plan, and reports terminal
// failure as a `{ type: "error" }` event rather than throwing, so a partial
// answer already delivered to the user is never lost.
